extracted.intended_audience: judges, lawyers, criminalists, penologists, and forensic observers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on reading bodily signs (face, hands, feet) and on the psychological/logical testing of evidence, testimony, and confessions for legal fact-finding. Emphasizes how a judge or investigator should interpret gestures and reconstruct evidential processes psychologically before presenting to a jury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gesture of resignation indicates innocence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not an empirical accident that the gesture of resignation is made regularly by innocent persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guilty tend to show other responses (catch at head, look toward heaven, grit teeth, rage, dull apathy). Resignation implies surrender of a value one had a claim on; a guilty person who has no claim to innocence will not show the emotion of resignation. Use resignation as supporting evidence of innocence, not as sole proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction of the brow signals intensive consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The contraction of the brow occurs when anything is dealt with intensively, increasing with the difficulty of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real intensive thought produces physiological signs (sharpened vision via forehead contraction). When a defendant/witness must recall a distant detail (e.g., an alibi) a sincere person will show genuine contraction and other signs of effort; a dishonest person will at best simulate 'thoughtfulness' without the proper earnest signs. Observe for authentic markers vs mere imitation to suspect false testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blank expression of the eyes indicates intuitive, absorbed thought
rubrics_metrics.description: That blank expression of the eyes only shows that its possessor is completely lost in his thoughts--this has nothing to do with sharp recollection and demands above all things being let alone or the belief of being so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This state is 'intuitive thought' or spiritual sight-seeing rather than analytic reconstruction. It often occurs when the witness is no longer listening but is reviewing life or the development of his deed; confessions are often easier to obtain in this condition if the interrogator keeps watchful eye contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction of brow + smile = disbelief/doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: That contraction of the brow signifies a condition of disgust is well known, but ... its combination with a smile, indicating disbelief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expression reliably signals disbelief or doubt; experimentally one finds oneself thinking 'that can't be true' when making it. It is common when confronting witnesses with defendants or witnesses with each other. Do not assume belief when this expression appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slight eyebrow elevation and brow contraction indicate embarrassment or need for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The close relation of the contraction of the brow with its early stage, a slight elevation of the eyebrows, is manifest ... it occurs under embarrassment ... upon the perception of something foreign and inexplicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to judge whether a defendant truly does not understand an argument: an innocent person may frown and listen attentively; a guilty person who already knows the facts often will not need to contract his brow, though he may feign attentiveness. Consider individual ability to perform such expressions (some cannot voluntarily do them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facial feature movement correlates with uplifting vs oppressive emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: All joyous and uplifting emotions (even astonishment) are succeeded by the raising of the skin of the forehead, the nostrils, the eyes, the eyelids, while sad and oppressing emotions have the contrary effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general rule helps interpret ambiguous expressions: upward movement suggests positive/joyous states; downward movement suggests sadness/oppression. Use as a heuristic, not absolute proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand physiognomy is significant and hard to simulate
rubrics_metrics.description: The physiognomy of the hand stands close to that of the face in significance and is in some relations of even greater importance, because the expression of the hand permits of no, or very slight, simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands may be cosmetically altered but not their fundamental physiognomy. Observers can often infer stable character or life-history from hands more reliably than from transient facial mimicry. Use hand observation as a corroborating source, especially when chirognomy and physiognomy agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands reveal occupation, ancestry, and past physical exertion
rubrics_metrics.description: People whose ancestors have worked with their hands possess heavy hands. Conversely, people whose ancestors have not worked hard with their hands possess small and fine hands ... hard work, piano playing, etc., should alter the form of a hand ... physical properties are hereditary and observable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the hand for signs of long-term manual labor, inherited racial/ethnic traits, or professional practice. Such signs can inform inferences about a person's background, but treat racial/general claims cautiously and corroborate with other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study hand-only movements beginning at the wrist for psychological inference
rubrics_metrics.description: For the study of those movements the hand of childhood is of little use ... I mean those that begin at the wrist and therefore occur in the hand only. ... This movement Darwin has observed even among kittens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-only movements (not arm-coordinated gestures) reveal desires (e.g., desire to possess, drawing toward oneself) and subtle emotional states. Observe adult, trained hands for these micro-movements; childhood hands are less diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual/temperamental differences in hand movements
rubrics_metrics.description: The masculine hand is generally too heavy and slow, clearly to exhibit the more refined movements; these are fully developed only in the feminine, particularly in the hands of vivacious, nervous, and spiritually excitable women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect finer, more revealing finger/ball-of-thumb manipulations among women; men may show cruder, slower indications. Use these tendencies to read concealed anger, nervousness, impatience, or pleasure in hand behavior, but avoid stereotyping individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feet and toes movements convey emotions (esp. in women)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toes reveal a great deal, particularly among women ... In anger ... the women press their toes closely to the ground. If they are embarrassed they turn the sole of their shoe slightly inwards... Impatience shows itself through alternating and swinging pressure of heel and toe ... Sensuality is always indicated when the foot is put forward and the shin bone lightly stretched out ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalogue observable cues: anger = toes pressed to ground; embarrassment = sole turned inwards; impatience = heel/toe alternation; defiance = toes raised so sole forward; sensuality = foot forward and toes drawn in. Use context and corroboration when interpreting these signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine hands of those claiming hard work but suspected of idleness (e.g., thieves, gamblers)
rubrics_metrics.description: In conclusion it ought to be kept in mind that the hands of all those people who claim to be hard workers but who really try to live without work, i.e. thieves, gamblers, etc., ought to be carefully examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mismatch between claimed occupation and hand condition may indicate deception about lifestyle. Use hand inspection as an investigatory lead, not definitive proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exaggeration; test observations of hand-language cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons believing in them must be warned against exaggeration and haste. The one advice that can be given is to study the language of the hand before officially ignoring it; not to decide immediately upon the value of the observations ... but to handle them cautiously and to test them with later experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect repeated, well-documented observations (photographs, known-character hands) and involve anatomists/experts before drawing systematized inferences. Treat individual observations as provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological conditions determine the manner and value of inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Inferences and theories are often constructed which are formally or logically absolutely free of error, yet psychologically full of errors that no logic whatever could correct. We have, therefore, to consider at least the most important conditions which determine the manner of our inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating another's inferences (or presenting evidence), examine the psychological processes that produced them. Logical form alone is insufficient; consider perception, habituation, presuppositions, and other psychological influences on evidence-gathering and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's duty: test evidence psychologically before giving it to the jury
rubrics_metrics.description: Nowadays more than ever, it is for the judge to test all evidence psychologically, to review what is only apparently clear, to fill out lacunae, and to surmount difficulties, before he permits the material ... to pass into the jury’s hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A responsible judge should not merely compile testimony but actively assess its psychological reliability, revise descriptions where necessary, and reconstruct processes so jurors receive only material that has been examined for hidden biases or presuppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local examinations must report what the examiner thought and represented to himself
rubrics_metrics.description: Every local examination ... must give an accurate picture of the mental process of him who made it. ... it must demonstrate what the examiner thought and represented to himself in order that the reader ... may have a chance to make corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local/court-site reports should not be treated as purely 'objective' lists of distances and facts; they must include the examiner's impressions and assumptions, and be reconstructed as they would appear if written with full knowledge, so later readers can evaluate potential bias or misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal formality is insufficient; evidence must also sustain logico-psychologic tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'source' of reasons and certainties must satisfy the legal demands not only formally but must sustain materially every possible test, whether circumstantial or logico-psychologic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a procedural checklist is satisfied (protocols, number of witnesses, confession recorded), each element must be examined for internal coherence, psychological plausibility, and susceptibility to error; otherwise 'form' may mask unreliable material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness testimony requires internal logical and psychological testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The utterance of witnesses is tested by its consistency with other evidence, but that is neither the only test nor the most valid, for there is always the more important internal test, in the first place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for inner contradictions within a witness's account, assess capacity/willingness to tell truth, and test statements on their own logical and psychological merits rather than relying solely on cross-consistency with other testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confessions are means of proof, not conclusive proof; motives must be established
rubrics_metrics.description: The confession must be accepted as a means of proof, not as proof, and this demands that it shall be consistent with the rest of the evidence, for in that way only can it become proof. The most certain foundation for the truth of confession in any case is the establishment of a clear motive for it--and that is rarely present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always investigate motives behind confessions. A confession without a clear, indubitable motive is suspect; analyze the confessor's inner life and circumstances to understand why they confessed. Use negation/apagogic reasoning to eliminate alternative motives where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial confessions require careful contextual interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial confessions are difficult ... because what is confessed appears doubtful in the light of what is not. ... such cases do not repay a great deal of troublesome examination ... but it is never indifferent whether a man pleads guilty or not guilty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider tactical motivations (hope of leniency, taking blame for others, legal knowledge). Even when partial confessions seem trivial to the current case, they may have significant evidential ramifications in future proceedings. Evaluate both immediate and long-term implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confessions implying guilt of another must be internally and psychologically scrutinized
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain definite confessions ... (c) Confessions implying the guilt of another ... it is most essential that the confession shall be internally tested, i.e. examined for logical and psychological consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a confession accuses others, scrutinize motive (e.g., malice, protection, coercion), internal consistency, possible benefits from shifting blame, and corroborating evidence. Treat such confessions with heightened skepticism and seek independent confirmation.
